strings: Table helper
Mission time! Help set the table for the next meal: plates, cups and spoons.
Great helping! A family table is a happy table.
Count how many people will eat.
Put one plate, one cup and one spoon for each person.
Let your child carry only unbreakable things if they are small. Counting places is good number practice.
Thank-you mission
Find someone who helped you today and say: thank you!
A thankful heart makes others smile.
Prayer for a friend
Think of a friend. Close your eyes and ask God to bless them today.
Praying for others is a gift you can give every day.
Your child may want to tell you who they prayed for. Listening is enough; no need to check the words.
Secret kindness
Do one kind thing for someone in your family, without being asked.
Kindness is a superpower. Well done, Emmavenger!
Draw a thank-you
Draw one thing you are thankful for today. Show it to a grown-up.
What a lovely picture of thanks!
Plant friend
With a grown-up, give a plant a little water. Plants need care, just like us.
You helped something grow today!
Stay close if the plant is outside or near water. Show how much water is enough.
Family thank-you time
Put the screens away and sit together for ten minutes.
A grown-up reads Psalm 136:1 from the family Bible.
Each person says one thing they want to thank God for today.
Finish with a short prayer together.
What was the best part of your day?
Who could we thank tomorrow?
Talk after a story
After your child finishes a story in the app, talk about it together.
Ask your child to tell you the story in their own words.
Ask one of the questions below, then share your own answer too.
Who was kind in the story?
What would you have done?
Play together sometimes
Children learn more from a screen when a grown-up joins in, talks about what they see and helps them use it in real life.
This week, sit with your child for one game or story and ask what they learned.
Screens off before bed
Paediatricians advise no screens in the hour before bedtime and keeping devices out of the bedroom at night.
Try a family thank-you time or a bedtime story read aloud instead.
